correctness.rationale: For the linearized bounded Neumann problem the modal trace is strictly negative under the stated kinetic condition, so instability is equivalent to negativity of the quadratic modal determinant \(D(z)=d_1d_2z^2-Bz+C\). When \(B>0\) and the discriminant is positive, negativity occurs only on the open continuous band between the two positive roots; a bounded interval is unstable exactly when one of the discrete values \(k^2/l^2\) lies inside that band. The inspected exact-arithmetic verifier reconstructs the coexistence point and coefficients and certifies the witness: the vertex is below 100, \(D(100)>0\), whereas \(D(4)<0\) and \(D(9)<0\). Thus the same kinetics satisfy the source's continuous-band condition but are stable for \(l=1/10\) and unstable in modes 2 and 3 for \(l=1\).
